title: Scheduling Order and Notice of Hearing (Docket No. 26-035-20)
text:
- BEFORE THE PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION OF UTAH - 

Application of PacifiCorp d/b/a Rocky 
Mountain Power for Approval and Report 
of the Sale of Washington Service Area 
and an Accounting Order 

DOCKET NO. 26-035-20 

SCHEDULING ORDER AND NOTICE OF 
HEARING 

ISSUED: April 21, 2026 

The Public Service Commission (PSC) held a scheduling conference in this 
docket on April 20, 2026, during which the parties in attendance stipulated to a 
schedule (“Stipulated Schedule”). 
The Division of Public Utilities (DPU) expressed concern about Rocky Mountain 
Power’s (RMP) request to include, in the schedule, a deadline for parties to propound 
discovery, noting DPU has experienced issues in the past with receiving appropriately 
supplemented or updated discovery responses. RMP pointed to Utah Admin. Code 
R746-1-501(3)(e), which contemplates that the PSC “may include in a scheduling 
order deadlines for[,]” among other things, “completing discovery.” RMP readily 
conceded that DPU has broad statutory authority to require RMP to provide 
information pertaining to matters within the PSC’s jurisdiction regardless of the 
existence of a proceeding before the PSC, and RMP emphasized its readiness to work 
with DPU to provide any information DPU requires. See, e.g., Utah Code § 54-4a-1(e). 
However, within the context of a specific docket, RMP insisted it is appropriate to 
include a deadline to propound discovery such that all parties have a reasonable 
opportunity to prepare for hearing. 
DOCKET NO. 26-035-20 

- 2 - 

The PSC concludes that inclusion of a deadline to propound discovery is 
reasonable and appropriate. Such a deadline does not restrict or otherwise interfere 
with DPU’s ability to exercise its broad statutory authority to seek information from 
RMP, which is not contingent on the existence of any particular proceeding before the 
PSC. 
However, the PSC also acknowledges DPU’s legitimate interest in ensuring that 
RMP supplements discovery responses whenever new or different information 
becomes available. The Utah Rules of Civil Procedure provide: “[i]f a party learns that 
a … [discovery] response is incomplete or incorrect in some important way, the party 
must timely serve on the other parties the additional or correct information” and must 
“state why the additional or correct information was not previously provided.” Utah R. 
Civ. P. 26(d)(5). 
Unless a party moves the PSC for formal discovery, the Utah Rules of Civil 
Procedure are persuasive, as opposed to mandatory, authority in proceedings before 
the PSC. Utah Admin. Code R746-1-105; R746-1-501. Given DPU’s legitimate interest 
in ensuring discovery responses are appropriately supplemented and RMP’s 
legitimate interest in establishing a deadline for propounding discovery in advance of 
the hearing, the PSC adopts RMP’s proposed discovery deadline, included in the 
schedule below, and expressly imposes an affirmative and continuing duty on all 
parties to supplement their discovery responses in this proceeding whenever new,

26(d)(5).

DISCOVERY 

Discovery turn-around times are 14 calendar days until November 20, 2026, 
and 7 calendar days thereafter. Parties shall serve discovery requests and responses 
on applicable parties by electronic mail. In the event a document produced in 
response to a discovery request cannot reasonably be transmitted by electronic mail,

the party disclosing the document shall provide an electronic copy of the document on 
CD (or, if an electronic copy is not available, a paper copy). 
NOTICE OF HEARING 

The PSC will conduct a hearing on Wednesday, January 13, 2027, through 
Friday, January 15, 2027, beginning at 9:00 a.m. each day of the hearing, Fourth Floor 
Hearing Room 403, Heber M. Wells Building, Salt Lake City, Utah. All parties must 
have their witnesses in attendance and prepared to testify. Any person desiring to 
attend this event must show government-issued photo identification to be admitted 
past the building security station. 
Individuals wishing to participate in the hearing remotely should contact the 
PSC at least two days in advance by calling (801) 530-6716 or (toll-free) 1-866-PSC-
UTAH (1-866-772-8824) to receive connection information and instructions. 

Individuals needing accommodations during the hearing should notify the PSC 
at 160 East 300 South, Salt Lake City, Utah 84111, (801) 530-6716, at least three 
working days prior to the hearing.
